dedupe_keys.name: systemisches kaskadenpotenzial von kritis teilsektoren expert survey dependency network of germany s 29 critical infrastructure subsectors izr 2019

description: This article operationalises the systemic cascade potential of the 29 subsectors of Germany's critical infrastructure system, meaning how strongly a failure in one subsector can spread through the dependencies of others. Hanna Christine Schmitt of the Institute of Spatial Planning at TU Dortmund wrote it as part of a doctoral thesis, and the Federal Institute for Research on Building, Urban Affairs and Spatial Development published it in Informationen zur Raumentwicklung in 2019. The data come from an online survey on dependencies between KRITIS subsectors, run on SoSci Survey in spring 2019 with at least three experts per subsector across the nine sectors of the national strategy, and are analysed as a network with centrality measures and a ranking. Electricity has the largest node and the most central position, ahead of information technology and telecommunications, while food and aviation show why centrality alone misleads. Coverage is Germany at the level of subsectors, with no locations. Format and access: a German-language PDF article with network figures. Licence: not stated; free. Caveats: dependency strengths are expert judgements, and the full survey matrix is not published as a file. It gives a national dependency structure for cascading failure and network models. A related catalogue record is the inter 3 guide to KRITIS interdependency analysis.
